Comic Con  
Tullamore library will host the first Comic 
con on Saturday 18th May.  This will 
include a number of stalls, cosplay 
competition for adults, children and 
families, Viking Reenactment group from 
Rhode, workshops, game stations and 
much more.  The library will open from 
10am – 5pm for this event.

ENVIRONMENT / WATER SERVICES:  
Litter and Waste complaints 2019 
Waste complaints thus far 55, Litter 
complaints 250, this includes 77 clean-ups 
carried out by local groups. We continue to 
work with Tidy Towns & Community 
Groups on the National Spring Clean 
Initiative. 
We 
provide 
groups 
with 
equipment to assist in the clean-ups and 
arrange collection of waste collected. Green 
school assessments have been completed & 
submitted to An Taisce for consideration.   
Schools will be notified of the outcome in the 
coming weeks. The Litter Management Plan 
will be considered by the Councillors at the 
April meeting. 
Water Quality 
Water Quality staff continue to participate in 
the Water Framework Directive Operational 
Committees in both the Eastern & Midlands 
Region, and also the South East Region.  The 
implementation 
of 
the 
River 
Basin 
Management Plan for Ireland 2018-2021 is 
progressing with the LA Shared Services 
Catchment Assessments Teams commencing 
work on the ground in the Priority Areas for 
Action (PAA). The Silver River catchment 
in Kilcormac will be assessed by the 
Catchment Assessment Team.   
 
 
 
 
 
WATER SERVICES 
Capital Projects 
Works in Mountbolus and Brosna South are 
completed.     Works are ongoing in Crinkle. 
The design and build contract for the major 
upgrade of the Tullamore and Birr Water is 
progressing. Design for Clonin, Croghan, 
Blundelwood, Clonmullen Lane & Newtown 
is progressing. The Tullamore Drainage Area 
Plan 2018 will inform sewerage network 
upgrade going forward.  
 
Consultants have been appointed to look at 
storm water design in Cloghan and Shinrone 
– this is at design stage at present. Ground 
Investigation is being completed in Cloghan 
and Shinrone for tendering purpose. This is 
planned to go out to tender in Q2 2019. 
Upgrade 
works 
at 
Banagher 
Water 
Treatment 
plant 
are 
complete, 
commissioning works are being agreed and 
implemented. 
Watermain 
Rehabilitation 
works 
are 
reaching completion at Mucklagh and 
Screggan.  Works have commenced in 
Crinkle and Mountbolus with Brosna South 
to commence in January. 
Belmont Rising Main is completed; this will 
reduce tankering costs into the future. 
Tullamore Sewer Rehabilitation works have 
commenced & 505 of the works have been 
completed to date.

ROADS:  
The Road Works Programme for 2019 was 
presented at the Council meeting of 25th 
March 2019. The 2019 budget of €14.63m 
includes €2.96m from the TII for National 
Roads, €9.88m from the Department of 
Transport, Tourism and Sport for Regional 
and Local Roads and €1.79m in own 
resources. The Roads Section and three 
Municipal 
Districts 
will 
deliver 
the 
programme in 2019.  
 
LOCAL & COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT 
The Local Community Development 
Committee  
(LCDC) met on 14th March 2019.  Agenda 
items included the Rural Development 
LEADER Programme 2014-2020, National 
Community Weekend and Local Migrant 
Integration Strategy.   
    
Local Migrant Integration Strategy 
It was agreed by the members that the LCDC 
would lead the development of a Local 
Migrant Integration Strategy for Offaly.  It is 
anticipated that this Strategy will be 
completed by June 2019 and forwarded to the 
members of Offaly County Council for final 
adoption at the July 2019 monthly Council 
meeting.   
 
National Community Weekend  
Members of the 
LCDC approved a 
recommendation from the Sub-Committee to 
allocate bursaries and were informed that the 
events taking place over 4th-6th May 2019 
are to be known nationally as “The Big 
Hello”.  The main Offaly event will take 
place in Lough Boora Parklands on Sunday 
5th May 2019 with activities including food, 
art exhibits, music, arts and crafts, games and 
sporting activities for all the family.  The 
event management plan for the day is 
currently being prepared with extensive 
marketing and promotion to take place over 
the coming weeks.       
 
Age Friendly Strategy  
The Age Friendly Alliance Meeting was held 
on March 7th Updates were given from 
Offaly Sports Partnership, Local Link 
Laois/Offaly, HSE, An Garda Siochana, 
OLDC and the Offaly Older Persons 
Network. Projects highlighted included the 
Intergenerational Programme in conjunction 
with Music Generation Offaly Westmeath; 
Bealtaine Festival and the Offaly Explorer 
venture in conjunction with Local Link. The 
Offaly Older Person’s Forum Housing 
Showcase took place on 4th April 2019 in the 
Darmagh Centre, Tullamore. Offaly Co. Co. 
staff from the Housing & Community & 
Culture were in attendance. 
 
Public Participation Network  
The Green Offaly Environmental Trust 
Consultations took place in Birr, Ferbane, 
Tullamore & Daingean. These were well 
attended with considerable interest in the 
Environment in terms of Community 
sustainability. The results of Community 
Planning took place in Lusmagh with OLDC, 
Offaly PPN & Offaly Co. Co staff in 
attendance. Discussions took place with the 
arts office to ensure Bealtaine events take 
place this year and with a view to planning 
towards a larger project in 2020. The 
Community Watch meeting was facilitated 
with good attendance and the establishment 
of the establishment of a Community 
Federation to manage CCTV in communities 
across the county.  
 
Comhairle na nOg  
The Executive met on 27th March and 
decided on their 2019 Project under the 
theme ‘Promoting Positive Mental Health – 
Dealing with Exam Stress and Anxiety’. 4

Programmes  
Staff of the Sports Partnership (Community 
Sports Development Officer and Sports 
Inclusion Development Officer), the south 
Offaly sports hub and partner agencies (FAI 
and Leinster Rugby via their development 
officers) continue to deliver sport and 
physical activity programmes for children, 
young people, people with disabilities, 
adults, older adults and the least active across 
the county. 
Programme reports on the Integrated 
Academy for Athletics Performance and the 
Healthy Ireland funded daily 20 min physical 
activity programme in schools are currently 
being finalised and will be available for 
publication in the coming weeks.

project 
in

currently being purchased, and introductory

with the aim of launching the Edenderry

LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE 
Upcoming Events and New Initiatives 
Offaly’s Network of Entrepreneurs (O.N.E.) 
Offaly’s Network of Entrepreneurs (O.N.E.) 
is free to join and is for anyone in business. 
If you are thinking of setting up your own 
business, you are also more than welcome. 
Benefits include: Members only Discount 
Card. Offaly's Network of Entrepreneurs is 
free to join. Next meeting 29th of April and 
the topic is “What is Social Selling? How can 
it deliver you results? The speaker is Greg 
Fry. 
 
Prepare your Business for Customs 
Workshop 9th May 
FREE workshop in the Tullamore Court 
Hotel on the 9th May covering how export & 
import customs procedures. This workshop 
will cover how export and import customs 
procedures on trade with ‘Third Countries’ 
apply, how tariffs work and the need to 
correctly classify your goods. There is now 
an urgent need to prepare your company for 
customs with this one-day interactive 
workshop. Regardless of a hard or soft 
Customs Brexit, goods to/from the UK or 
transiting through the UK, will be subject to

May 2019 
The event will see small food and drink 
producers, supported by the Local Enterprise 
Offices, showcase their best products, giving 
buyers the unique opportunity to taste 
excellence in Irish food and drink. The

Wednesday 10 April.  
 
Get Business Brexit Ready 
Local Enterprise Office Offaly has a range of 
supports to help Offaly businesses to address 
issues and maximise potential opportunities; 
Brexit 
Loan 
Scheme 
Information 
Pack -  Eligible businesses can now apply for 
the €300 million Brexit Loan Scheme. The 
Brexit Loan Scheme, which was announced 
in the 2018 budget, will provide affordable 
financing to businesses that are either 
currently impacted by Brexit or will be in the 
future.  The Scheme, which will be delivered 
by the Strategic Banking Corporation of 
Ireland (SBCI) through commercial lenders 
will make €300 million available to eligible 
businesses with up to 499 employees at an 
interest rate of 4% or less.

LIBRARY SERVICES 
Spring into Storytime  
April is the month for the national initiative 
of Spring into Storytime.  There will be 
storytelling sessions in all 8 branches around 
the county.  This is part of the Right to Read 
programme.  The launch of the programme 
will be in Banagher on Thursday 11th April.  
Each small branch will have one storytime 
session- Banagher, Daingean, Ferbane and 
Kilcormac.  Clara will host two storytime 
sessions and Birr, Edenderry and Tullamore 
will host four during the month of April 
 
Tradfest Tullamore  
The library will be hosting a family day on 
Sunday 14th April as part of the new festival 
– Tradfest Tullamore.  The library will open 
as part of the programme with events and 
music for all the family.  The library will be 
open to the public from 11am – 2pm on 
Sunday for this event.

Bealtaine 2019 
The Library, Arts officer and the PPN officer 
are organising a number of events for 
Bealtaine.  These events include the launch 
of the Tovertafel or Magic Table in 
Tullamore.  The Tovertafel is a fun care 
innovation that connects older people in the 
late stage of their dementia journey with each 
other and with their surroundings, all the 
while stimulating movement. The beautiful 
games were developed specifically for the 
target group and can be played both 
independently and under supervision. 
 
Comic Con  
Tullamore library will host the first Comic 
con on Saturday 18th May.  This will include 
a number of stalls, cosplay competition for 
adults, 
children 
and 
families, 
Viking 
Reenactment group from Rhode, workshops, 
game stations and much more.  The focus is 
to demonstrate the local interest and talents 
to the Animation and Comic or Graphic 
Novels scene.  The library will open from 
10am – 5pm for this event.   
 
 
CORPORATE SERVICES 
Hungarian Ambassador Visit 
The Hungarian Ambassador to Ireland, His 
Excellency István Pálffy and his wife Mrs. 
Judit Toth visited Offaly County Council on 
11th March 2019. The Ambassador was 
greeted by Cathoairleach Danny Owens, Mr. 
Sean Murray Director of Services, Mr. 
Declan Conlon, Head of Finance and Mary 
Flynn Kenny, A/Senior Executive Officer. 
His Excellency was brought on a tour of 
Lough Boora and the Tullamore Dew 
Heritage Centre. 
 
 
 
Register of Electors 
The Register of Electors 2019 / 2020, 
published on 1st February 2019, became the 
Live Register of Electors on the 15th 
February 2019.   The closing date for the 
receipt of Special/Postal applications is 28th 
April 2019 and the closing date for receipt of 
Supplement applications is 7th May 2019. 
 
NOTICE OF ELECTION 
An election of members for each of the local 
electoral areas of Offaly County Council is 
about to be held. Nomination papers may be 
obtained during the usual office hours. A 
person may nominate himself/herself as a 
candidate or may, with his/her consent, be 
nominated by a proposer who is registered as 
a local government elector in the local 
electoral area of the local authority for which 
he/she proposes to nominate the candidate. 
A nomination paper from a candidate of a 
registered political party must have a 
certificate of political affiliation attached 
which must be produced to me with his/her 
completed nomination paper. If no certificate 
is attached, the candidate must, before the 
latest time for receiving nominations, either- 
 secure 15 assents to the nomination 
by way of statutory declarations by 
local government electors registered 
in the relevant local electoral area
